key: a pattern A is more sturdy
stem: If a street light of mass M is suspended from the end of a uniform rod of length L in the different possible patterns as shown in figure, then — in (A) the cable runs from the wall to the far end of the rod (distance L from the hinge), in (B) to the point at 3L/4 and in (C) to the point at L/2. (a) pattern A is more sturdy (b) pattern B is more sturdy (c) pattern C is more sturdy (d) all will have same sturdiness —

A cylinder is given angular velocity ω 0 and kept on a horizontal rough surface. The initial velocity is zero. Find out distance travelled by the cylinder before it performs pure rolling and work done by friction forces. —

A cubical block of side 30 cm is placed on a rough horizontal surface of coefficient of friction 0.6. At what minimum height above the ground, a horizontal force must be applied on the block so that it starts toppling before slipping? —

A uniform rod of mass m and length ℓ can rotate freely on a smooth horizontal plane about a vertical axis hinged at point H. A point mass having same mass m coming with an initial speed u perpendicular to the rod, strikes the rod in-elastically at its free end. Find out the angular velocity of the rod just after collision? —

A wedge in the form of equilateral triangle is placed on a rough horizontal surface as shown in the figure (a horizontal force F is applied at the apex P, the base QS resting on the ground). For what value of coefficient of friction, can the block topple without slipping? —

A disc is rolling, the velocity of its centre of mass is V cm , then which one will be correct? (a) The velocity of highest point is 2V cm and point of contact is zero (b) the velocity of highest point is 2V cm and point of contact is V cm (c) the velocity of highest point is 2V cm and point of contact is V cm (d) the velocity of highest point is 2V cm and point of contact is 2V cm —

key: d converts translational energy to rotational energy
stem: A drum of radius R and mass M, rolls down without slipping along an inclined plane of angle θ. The frictional force: (a) decreases the rotational and translational motion (b) dissipates energy as heat (c) decreases the rotational motion (d) converts translational energy to rotational energy —

A tube of length L is filled completely with an incompressible liquid of mass M and closed at both the ends. The tube is then rotated in a horizontal plane about one of its ends with uniform angular velocity ω. The force exerted by the liquid at the other end is: (a) MLω²/2 (b) ML²ω/2 (c) MLω² (d) ML²ω²/2 —

key: d No relation between h and R
stem: A solid sphere of radius R is placed on a smooth horizontal surface. A horizontal force ‘F’ is applied at height ‘h’ from the lowest point. For the maximum acceleration of centre of mass, which is correct? (a) h = R (b) h = 2R (c) h = 0 (d) No relation between h and R —

key: c up the incline while ascending as well as descending
stem: A cylinder rolls up an inclined plane, reaches some height and then rolls down without slipping throughout these motions. The direction of the frictional force acting on the cylinder are: (a) up the incline while ascending and down the incline while descending (b) down the incline while ascending and up the incline while descending (c) up the incline while ascending as well as descending (d) down the incline while ascending as well as descending —

A solid cylinder of mass 3 kg rolling on a horizontal surface with velocity 4 m/s. It collides with a horizontal spring of force constant 200 N/m. The maximum compression produced in the spring will be: (a) 0.7 m (b) 0.2 m (c) 0.5 m (d) 0.6 m —

The ratio of the accelerations for a solid sphere (mass ‘m’ and radius ‘R’) rolling down an incline plane of angle ‘θ’ without slipping and slipping down the incline without rolling is: (a) 5 : 7 (b) 2 : 3 (c) 2 : 5 (d) 7 : 5 —
The radius of a rotating sphere decreases by 2% keeping the mass constant, the change in its rotational kinetic energy? (a) 2% (b) 1% (c) 4% (d) 8% —
A torque of 12 Nm acts for 3 seconds. What is the angular impulse? (a) 9 Ns (b) 12 Ns (c) 15 Ns (d) 36 Ns —
If initial angular momentum is 20 kg⋅m²/s and final is 35 kg⋅m²/s, what is angular impulse? (a) 55 (b) 20 (c) 15 (d) 30 —
A torque of 8 Nm acts on a body for 4 seconds. If moment of inertia is 2 kg⋅m², find the angular velocity acquired. (a) 8 rad/s (b) 12 rad/s (c) 16 rad/s (d) 20 rad/s —

A solid cylinder of mass M and radius R rolls down an inclined plane of height (3/40) m and inclination θ. What is the speed (in ms −1 ) of its centre of mass when the cylinder reaches the bottom of the inclined plane? Given: g = 10 ms −2 —

A particle of mass m is released from rest at point A falling parallel to the vertical y-axis. Its angular momentum after falling through distance h about O is (O is the origin, A lies on the x-axis at a distance a from O, and B is the point reached after the fall): (a) ma√(2gh) (b) (m/a)√(2gh) (c) ma/gh (d) mh/ag —

A merry-go-round, made of a ring-like platform of radius R and mass M, is revolving with angular speed ω. A person of mass M is standing on it. At one instant, the person jumps off the round radially away from the centre of the round as seen from the round. The speed of the round afterwards is: (a) ω (b) 2ω (c) ω/2 (d) zero —
A 20 N force is applied at 6 cm height to a block of mass 4 kg. Find the value of ‘a’ to prevent toppling. (a) 2.5 cm (b) 3.0 cm (c) 4.0 cm (d) 5.0 cm —

A rod of mass m and length ℓ is translating with velocity v. Its angular momentum about O is (from the figure the rod is vertical, its lower end a height ℓ above the x-axis, and it moves along +x): (a) mvℓ(−K̂) (b) 2mvℓ(−K̂) (c) (3/2)mvℓ(−K̂) (d) ½mvℓ(−K̂) —

A disc is rolling without slipping, find its angular momentum about point O (O is the origin on the ground, the disc’s centre moves with velocity υ along +x): (a) ½mRv K̂ (b) (5/2)mRv K̂ (c) (7/2)mRv(−K̂) (d) (3/2)mRv(−k̂) —

The angular momentum of a sphere about point O as shown in fig. is (the sphere of mass m and radius R has centre velocity υ along +x and spins with ω = υ/2R in the forward-rolling sense; O is the origin on the ground): (a) (7/5)mRvK̂ (b) (6/5)mRvK̂ (c) −(7/5)mRvK̂ (d) −(6/5)mRvK̂ —

A sphere of mass m and radius R is rolling on the ground as shown, find its angular momentum about O (the centre moves with υ along +x while the figure marks ω = υ/R in the anticlockwise sense): (a) (6/5)mRvK̂ (b) −(3/5)mRvK̂ (c) (3/5)mRvK̂ (d) −(6/5)mRvK̂ —

Find angular momentum of ring of mass m and radius R as shown in fig. (the ring’s centre moves with υ along +x and it spins with ω = υ/R clockwise; the point O lies on the same horizontal line as the centre, to its left): (a) Zero (b) mRv (c) 2mRv (d) 3mRv —

A rod of mass m and length ℓ is doing combined motion. Its angular momentum about O is (from the figure the rod’s centre moves with υ along +x while the rod spins with ω = 4υ/R, and O lies a perpendicular distance ℓ/4 below the line of υ): (a) (7/12)mvℓ (b) (5/12)mvℓ (c) (7/6)mvℓ (d) (5/6)mvℓ —

A linear impulse J acts on the rod of mass m and length ℓ hinged about one end as shown in fig. The angular impulse acts on the rod about hinge point is (the rod hangs down from the hinge, J is horizontal along +x at the free lower end, y is up): (a) JℓK̂ (b) −(Jℓ/2)K̂ (c) (Jℓ/2)K̂ (d) −JℓK̂ —
A linear impulse J acts on the rod of mass m and length ℓ hinged about one end as shown in fig, the angular velocity of rod just after impulse is: (a) 3J/mℓ (b) 4J/mℓ (c) 2J/mℓ (d) 3J/mℓ —

A small particle of mass m collides with a rod of mass 4m and length ℓ with velocity v and reflects back with velocity v/2. The angular impulse acted on rod about hinge point during collision (the rod hangs from a hinge at its top and the particle strikes its free lower end): (a) mvℓ (b) mvℓ/2 (c) 3mvℓ/2 (d) 5mvℓ/2 —

A small particle of mass m collides with a rod of mass 4m and length ℓ with velocity v and reflects back with velocity v/2, the angular velocity of rod just after collision is: (a) (3/4)(v/ℓ) (b) (3/8)(v/ℓ) (c) (9/8)(v/ℓ) (d) (15/8)(v/ℓ) —

A stone of mass 0.1 kg is projected with a velocity of 20√2 m/s from the origin of an xy co-ordinate axis system at an angle of 45° with the horizontal. The angular momentum of the stone about the origin after 1 second is (take g = 10 m/s²): (a) 10k̂ (kg m²/s) (b) −10î (kg m²/s) (c) 10î (kg m/s²) (d) 10ĵ (kg m/s²) —

A small particle of mass m is projected at an angle θ with the x-axis with an initial velocity υ 0 in the x-y plane as shown in the figure. At a time t < υ 0 sinθ/g, the angular momentum of the particle is: (a) ½mgυ 0 t²cosθ î (b) −mgυ 0 t²cosθ ĵ (c) mgυ 0 t²cosθ k̂ (d) −½mgυ 0 t²cosθ k̂ — 📝 PYQ: AIEEE 2010 Solution ↗

A mass M is supported by a massless and inextensible string wound round a uniform cylinder of mass M and diameter 2R. With what acceleration (in ms −2 ) shall the mass fall when released from rest? Given: g = 10 ms −2 —

Fig. shows a flywheel of radius 10 cm. Its moment of inertia about the rotation axis is 0.4 kg-m². A massless string passes over the flywheel and a mass 2 kg is attached at its lower end. Angular acceleration of the pulley is nearly: (a) 4.8 rad/s² (b) 6.2 rad/s² (c) 3.2 rad/s² (d) 9.6 rad/s² —

A bar of mass M and length L is in pure translatory motion with its centre of mass velocity v. It collides with and sticks to a second identical bar which is initially at rest. (Assume that it becomes one composite bar of length 2L). The angular velocity of the composite bar will be: (a) (3v/4L) clockwise (b) (4v/3L) clockwise (c) (3v/4L) counter clockwise (d) (v/L) counter clockwise —

A solid sphere is rolling purely on a rough horizontal surface (coefficient of kinetic friction = μ) with speed of centre = u. It collides inelastically with a smooth vertical wall at a certain moment, the coefficient of restitution being 1/2. The sphere will begin pure rolling after a time: (a) 3u/(7μg) (b) 2u/(7μg) (c) 3u/(5μg) (d) 2u/(5μg) —

A bullet of mass m moving with velocity u just grazes the top of a solid cylinder of mass m and radius R resting on a rough horizontal surface as shown in figure. Assuming that the cylinder rolls without slipping, then the final velocity of bullet is: (a) 8u/11 (b) 7u/17 (c) 5u/12 (d) 9u/13 —

A disc of mass M and radius R is rolling purely with centre’s velocity v 0 on a flat horizontal floor when it hits a step in the floor of height R/4. The corner of the step is sufficiently rough to prevent any slipping of the disc against itself. What is the velocity of the centre of the disc just after impact? (a) 4v 0 /5 (b) 4v 0 /7 (c) 5v 0 /6 (d) None —

key: a topple before sliding if μ > a/h ⚠
stem: A block with a square base (a×a) and height h, is placed on an inclined plane. The coefficient of friction is μ. The angle of inclination θ of the plane is gradually increased. The block will: (a) topple before sliding if μ > a/h (b) topple before sliding if μ < a/h (c) slide before toppling if μ > a/h (d) slide before toppling if μ < a/h —

A cylinder rotating at an angular speed of 50 rev/s is brought in contact with an identical stationary cylinder. Because of the kinetic friction, torques act on the two cylinders, accelerating the stationary one and decelerating the moving one. If the common magnitude of the acceleration and deceleration be one revolution per second square, how long will it take before the two cylinders have equal angular speed? —

A hollow smooth uniform sphere A of mass m rolls without sliding on a smooth horizontal surface. It collides head on elastically with another stationary smooth solid sphere B of the same mass m and same radius. The ratio of kinetic energy of B to that of A just after the collision is: (a) 1 : 1 (b) 2 : 3 (c) 3 : 2 (d) None —

A thin uniform square plate ABCD of side ‘a’ and mass m is suspended in vertical plane as shown in the figure. AE and BF are two massless inextensible strings. The line AB is horizontal. The tension in the string AE just after BF is cut is: (a) 2mg/5 (b) 3mg/5 (c) 3mg/7 (d) 4mg/7 —

A uniform solid square plate ABCD of mass m and side ‘a’ is moving in XY horizontal smooth plane. The velocity of centre of mass is v 0 (2î + 4ĵ) m/s. The end A of square plate is suddenly fixed by a pin, find the new velocity of centre of mass of square. (From the figure B is the top-left corner, C top-right, A bottom-left and D bottom-right.) —

A cylinder of mass m is kept on the edge of a plank of mass 2m and length 12 m, which in turn is kept on smooth ground. Coefficient of friction between the plank and the cylinder is 0.1. The cylinder is given an impulse which imparts it a velocity 7 m/s but no angular velocity. The time after which the cylinder falls off the plank is: (a) 2 s (b) 2.25 s (c) 2.5 s (d) 2.75 s —

key: v = Ft/m, ω = 6Ft/(ml), KE = 2F²t²/m, L cm = Flt/2
stem: A uniform rod of mass m and length l is struck at an end by a force F perpendicular to the rod for a short time interval t. Calculate (a) the speed of the centre of mass, (b) the angular speed of the rod about the centre of mass, (c) the kinetic energy of the rod and (d) the angular momentum of the rod about the centre of mass after the force has stopped to act. Assume that t is so small that the rod does not appreciably change its direction while the force acts. —

Suppose the rod with the balls A and B of the previous problem is clamped at the centre in such a way that it can rotate freely about a horizontal axis through the clamp. The system is kept at rest in the horizontal position. A particle P of the same mass m is dropped from a height h on the ball B. The particle collides with B and sticks to it. (a) Find the angular momentum and the angular speed of the system just after the collision. (b) What should be the minimum value of h so that the system makes a full rotation after the collision? —

key: a, c 11 N before; 5 N just after
stem: [Multiple Correct] A uniform rod of mass M = 2 kg and length L is suspended by two smooth hinges 1 and 2 as shown in the figure. A force F = 4 N is applied downward at a distance L/4 from the hinge 2. Due to the application of force F, the hinge 2 breaks. At this instant, applied force F is also removed. The rod starts to rotate downward about hinge 1. (g = 10 m/s²). Choose the correct statement(s). (a) The reaction at hinge 1, before hinge 2 breaks, is 11 N (b) the reaction at hinge 1, before hinge 2 breaks, is 24 N (c) the reaction at hinge 1, just after breaking of hinge 2, is 5 N (d) the reaction at hinge 1, just after breaking of hinge 2 is 8 N —

[Multiple Correct] Rod B sticks to rod A on collision. Collision takes place on horizontal plane. Rod A (mass m, length L) is hinged at O and lies along the horizontal; rod B (mass m, length L) is perpendicular to it with its upper end at A’s free end, moving with velocity v 0 . Friction is absent everywhere. (a) Angular velocity of system just after collision is 2v 0 /5L (b) velocity of centre of mass of system just after collision is √(9/40)v 0 (c) centre of mass of system is at a distance √10L/4 from O (d) kinetic energy of system just after collision is (9/40)mv² —

key: a, b, c ω = 3v 0 /2ℓ; v 0,min = √(8gℓ/3); loss = Mv 0 ²/8
stem: [Multiple Correct] A uniform rod AB of length ℓ and mass M hangs from point A at which it is freely hinged in a car moving with velocity v 0 . The rod can rotate in vertical plane about the axis at A. If the car suddenly stops, (a) the angular speed ω with which the rod starts rotating is 3v 0 /2ℓ (b) the minimum value of v 0 , so that the rod completes the rotation is √(8gℓ/3) (c) loss of energy during the process is (1/8)Mv 0 ² (d) there is no loss of energy —

key: a, c, d ω′ = 13ω/32 reversed; v p = 7ωr/32; J pivot = 15mωr/32
stem: [Multiple Correct] A uniform rod of length 2r and mass m is rotating in a horizontal plane about a fixed pivot through centre at a steady speed of ω. A particle of mass m moving with speed ωr/4 strikes an end of the rod perpendicularly. The rod and the particle are moving towards each other and the coefficient of restitution is 1/2. (a) The new angular speed of the rod is 13ω/32 in clockwise direction as seen from the above (b) the new angular speed of the rod is 13ω/32 in anti-clockwise direction as seen from the above (c) the new speed of the particle is 7ωr/32 (d) the impulsive reaction at the pivot is 15mωr/32 —
